title: Synthesis and Tribological Characteristics of High-Performance Self-Lubricating CoCrFeNiMo<sub>x</sub>-Ni/MoS<sub>2</sub>-Ag-Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> Composites.

recollection.starting_material: Probably equiatomic Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo high-entropy-alloy (HEA) powders blended with Ni powder and solid-lubricant additives MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3.
recollection.intervention: Likely consolidated the blended powders by spark-plasma sintering or hot pressing, followed by heat treatment, to obtain a bulk self-lubricating composite.
recollection.structure: A dense, multiphase composite consisting of an FCC CoCrFeNiMo_x (or Ni-rich) metallic matrix with dispersed MoS2 platelets, Ag particles, and fine Cr2O3 oxides providing a lubricious/oxidation-resistant surface layer during sliding.
recollection.mechanism: Under sliding, MoS2 shears easily, Ag forms a ductile transfer film, and Cr2O3 contributes a hard, stable oxide layer; their combined action lowers friction and wear while the HEA matrix offers high strength and thermal stability.
recollection.results: My best guess is that the composite showed a friction coefficient around 0.08-0.15 at room temperature, remaining below ~0.25 up to 600 °C, with wear rates on the order of 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹—substantially better than the unreinforced HEA or Ni matrix. Hardness likely exceeded 350–400 HV, and strength/ductility were retained after high-temperature tests.

score.note: The recollection correctly guesses powder consolidation by SPS and gives a broadly plausible FCC multiphase composite and generic MoS2/Ag lubrication mechanisms. However, it misses the central intervention of varying Mo content (x = 0.2, 0.5, 1), the Mo-induced lattice distortion and σ-phase formation, and the high-temperature silver-molybdate/NiO glaze mechanism. Its friction and wear estimates are substantially inconsistent with the reported temperature-dependent peaks and values; only the rough hardness range is plausible.
